play_evaluation_accepted_and_used_by_g1.name: EVALUATION_RULES
play_evaluation_accepted_and_used_by_g1.governs: every G1 Stratego game played under P18-D002 and P18-D003, and the accepted play gates of Phases 9, 11B, 12 and 15

common_to_both.note: the two presets differ in exactly two fields: battleless_move_limit and context

reasons: comparability: Gate G1 is closed and was measured under battleless 200; evaluating G3/G4 under 100 would make them non-comparable to the accepted baseline for no gain

precedent: every accepted play gate since Phase 4 uses EVALUATION_RULES and stratego/evaluation/match_spec.py defaults rules=EVALUATION_RULES at four sites; naming training rules for a play lane is the anomaly

avoids introducing additional early censoring: the battleless limit binds hardest between comparable players (13.09% / 13.38% of vs_init games versus about 1% of random-opponent games at limit 200), which is the regime G3/G4 contrasts live in. Keeping 200 changes nothing about how those games terminate; moving to 100 would censor continuations earlier and weakly increase the number of games terminated as battleless draws, with an effect on variance, effect size and power that is unknown. This is a reason to decline an unnecessary, uncharacterised change to the measurement - NOT a claim that 200 has a demonstrated power advantage over 100
separation of concerns: training rules govern corpus generation and evaluation rules govern measurement; one identity each prevents a change on one side from silently altering the other

alternative_rejected.option: adopt battleless_move_limit 100 for play evaluation to match the training corpus
alternative_rejected.why_not: breaks comparability with the closed G1 result, departs from every accepted play gate in the project, and introduces additional early censoring whose effect on the measurement has not been characterised. The last point is a reason for caution, not evidence that the alternative measures worse

observed_terminations_at_limit_200.reading: the 4000 absolute limit is a safety backstop that never fired; the battleless limit is the binding rule and is active in about ten times as many games between comparable players as against a random opponent. This locates where the rule is active; it does not indicate which limit measures better

effect_of_changing_the_battleless_limit.defensible_conclusion: reducing the battleless limit from 200 to 100 censors continuations earlier, so the number of games terminated as battleless draws weakly increases or is preserved; it cannot decrease
effect_of_changing_the_battleless_limit.draws_are_not_signal_free: the accepted effective win rate is EWR = (W + 0.5*D)/N (stratego/evaluation/statistics.py lines 11 and 98-107), so a draw scores 0.5 and contributes to a paired effective-win-rate difference like any other scored outcome; every draw=true row in the G1 receipts carries candidate_score 0.5
effect_of_changing_the_battleless_limit.draw_share_and_power: a higher draw share does NOT necessarily reduce statistical power; the effect runs through both the effect size and the variance of the paired differences and is not determined by the draw share alone
effect_of_changing_the_battleless_limit.power_comparison_status: UNKNOWN - the exact effect of the rule change on variance, effect size and power cannot be determined without a predeclared comparison, which would require playing games and is out of scope and unauthorized
